title: Knowledge Topology and the First Passage to Usable Hypotheses: A Readout Theory of Discovery Time and Direction

equations.section: 3.1 Knowledge organization is a domain readout
equations.meaning: Knowledge organization represented as a bounded, question-conditioned readout: accessible concept inventory, relation set, finite access weights, and relation provenance.

equations.section: 3.2 From access to a usable hypothesis
equations.text: U_{A,t}(Q) = { [H] in H^disc_{A,t}(Q) : W_t(H) >= w0,  exists u in U_{D,t} with Delta_u(H,H') > 0 for at least one live rival H' }
equations.meaning: Usable-for-inquiry target class: a readout-discriminable candidate must meet a warrant floor and admit at least one accessible discriminating action against a rival.

equations.section: 3.2 From access to a usable hypothesis
equations.meaning: Non-collapse: usability for inquiry is not truth; a usable hypothesis can later fail.

equations.text: tau_U = inf{ n >= 0 : Gamma_Q(S_n) in U_{A,n}(Q) }
equations.meaning: First passage: the earliest step/time at which the semantic-access trajectory enters the usable set.

equations.text: T_U(G^K, Q) = E[ tau_U | G^K, Q ]
equations.meaning: Expected first-passage time to a usable hypothesis given a declared knowledge organization and question.

equations.text: pi^{first}_{G^K,Q}(C_j) = Pr[ H_{tau_U} = C_j | G^K, Q ]
equations.meaning: Discovery-direction distribution: probability that a given usable readout class is the one reached first.
Jensen-Shannon divergence used as one finite diagnostic for comparing first-hit distributions between two organizations.

equations.label: H1
equations.section: 5 Central Hypothesis and Propositions (H1 - Organization-to-first-passage hypothesis)
equations.meaning: Under content-matched task/reader, changing knowledge organization changes the distribution of first-passage time to a usable hypothesis, for at least some task classes.

equations.text: P_Q(G^K) = < T_U, H(pi^{first}), D_H, W, C_escape >
equations.meaning: Joint evaluation profile for an organization: first-passage time, directional entropy, discriminable-class diversity, warrant, and restructuring/escape cost.

equations.label: H2
equations.meaning: Content-matched organizations can change which usable readout class is encountered first (a directional, not merely speed, claim).
Predicted (sign not fixed in advance) effect of graph-structured context on first-passage time.
Predicted effect of graph-structured context on the discovery-direction divergence.
Non-collapse rule: a shorter first-passage time does not imply higher warrant, which does not imply truth.
Schematic placement of organization within the companion imagination architecture: it changes the access kernel/topology feeding first-passage time and direction toward the usable set.
Restated central proposal: knowledge organization conditions the distribution of first-passage time and the first-hit direction to a usable hypothesis, sign unfixed.
